chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Umar ibn Yazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

There was a man among the Children of Israel who supplicated to Allah that He grant him a son for three years. When he saw that Allah was not answering him, he said, 'O Lord! Am I far from You, so You do not hear me, or are You close to me, so You do not answer me?'

He said: So a visitor came to him in his dream and said, 'You have been supplicating to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for three years with an obscene tongue, an arrogant heart that is not pious, and an intention that is not sincere. So desist from your obscenities, let your heart fear Allah, and let your intention be improved.'
He said: So the man did that, then supplicated to Allah, and a son was born to him.
ai.seo_question: Why was a man's supplication for a son rejected for three years according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* under 'The Obscenities,' this hadith illustrates the Shia principle that the efficacy of *dua* depends not only on the request but on the spiritual purity of the supplicant. The rejection is attributed to a triad of defects: an obscene tongue (*lisan*), an arrogant heart (*qalb*), and insincere intention (*niyyah*), highlighting that internal states directly influence divine response. This narrative serves as a practical guide for believers to examine their character and sincerity before seeking divine favor.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Umar Bin Yazeed, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘There was a man among the Children of Israel who supplicated to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> for three years that He<sup>azwj</sup> should Grace him with a son. So when he saw that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is not Answering him, said, ‘O Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! Am I so remote from You<sup>azwj</sup>, so You<sup>azwj</sup> are not Hearing me, or are You<sup>azwj</sup> close to me, but You<sup>azwj</sup> are not Answering me?’

He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘So a comer came to him in his dream and he said, ‘You have been supplicating to Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic since the last three years by an obscene tongue and an arrogant heart, nor fearful, and an intention without sincerity. So remove yourself from your obscenities, and fear Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> in your heart, and improve your intention’.
He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘So the man did that, then supplicated to Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, and a son was born unto him’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn Mahbub from ‘Umar ibn Yazid from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“In the tribe of Israel there was a man who prayed to Allah for a son for three years. When he found that Allah did not answer his prayer, he then asked, ‘O Lord, am I far away from You and You do not hear me or You are close to me but do not answer me?’

The Imam said, ‘Someone came in his dream and said, ‘You have prayed to Allah, the Majestic, the Glorious, for three years in an obscene language, with an oppressive heart that is impious and with untrue intentions. Stay away from obscenity, be pious before Allah and make your intention to be good.’
The Imam said, ‘The man followed the instruction, and prayed to Allah, only then a son was born to him. ’”
